title: Fallback variant parity sweeper: tokenizer, KV and toolchain maintenance
creator: Riley Chen
description: We need an operational sweep to ensure fallback model variants are compatible across tokenization, context handling, and runtime tooling (KV cache, prompt preprocessors, function/tool calling hooks). The goal is to reduce mismatches when smart routing switches requests between primary and fallback models (by region, tier, or capacity) for the hosted API and Dedicated modes. This ticket defines a maintenance plan: expand the compatibility matrix, add automated parity checks in CI, update model onboarding checklists, and implement runtime guards that detect and gracefully handle tokenizer/context mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix updated to include tokenization scheme, special token mapping (BOS/EOS/PAD), max context, and KV layout for all active fallback variants
Automated CI job (parity-sweeper) that runs tokenization + roundtrip tests across model pairs and fails on >0.5% tokenization delta for canonical prompts
Runtime guard added: if tokenizer/context mismatch risk detected for a request route, route is tagged and fallback is rate-limited until an automatic remediation or manual rollout
Onboarding checklist and model manifest fields augmented to declare tokenizer name, vocab hash, eos/pad ids, and KV schema version
Documentation and runbook published (Confluence) with remediation steps, rollback commands, and a postmortem template
tasks: Inventory active fallback variants and extract tokenizer/vocab metadata into a canonical CSV
Define tokenization delta metric and implement token-level diff tool (CLI + small library)
Build CI job that executes canonical prompt set through model pairs and records tokenization diffs
Add model manifest fields: tokenizer_name, vocab_sha256, eos_id, pad_id, kv_schema_version
Implement runtime detection: when routing to fallback, validate manifest parity and attach flags to trace/span
Update Model Onboarding doc and the SDKs to surface manifest validation errors
Create remediation playbook and add to Console runbook section; add dashboard panel for parity failures
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Model Onboarding, QA. Agreed canonical prompt set composed of 200 prompts across chat, code, and completion workloads.
2026-02-25: PoC token-diff tool implemented (python) and run against 12 model pairs — found 3 pairs with EOS mismatch causing trailing token shifts.
2026-03-02: Runtime team drafted a lightweight manifest schema; shared for review. Found ambiguity around KV schema versioning (needs semantic versioning).
2026-03-07: PM review (Diane Alvarez) requested explicit handling for tool-calling frames; Design suggested adding a transformer that normalizes tool frame tokens before comparison.
2026-03-10: CI job prototype merged to feature branch; failing cases surfaced internally. Plan: expand canonical prompts to cover function/tool boundaries and code snippets next week.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Mismatches cause subtle generation drift leading to customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: block automatic fallback for routes with high mismatch risk and add metric alerts.
Risk: CI parity runs increase pipeline time. Mitigation: schedule nightly parity-sweeper with sample sets, keep fast smoke tests in PRs.
Risk: Larger models change tokenization semantics during quantization/transform. Mitigation: require manifest vocab_sha256 and a binary-compatibility gate on rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-diff library covering BPE merges, unknown token handling, and special-token remapping
Integration test that spins up two variants in CI and runs canonical prompt set, asserting tokenization delta thresholds
Chaos test: simulate routing switch in staging and assert no uncaught tokenizer exceptions and acceptable end-to-end output delta metrics
Add telemetry: tokenization_delta histogram, parity_failure_rate by model-pair, and routing-block incidents
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): run parity-sweeper nightly for top 10 traffic model pairs; flag issues but do not block fallback. Duration: 1 week.
Stage 2 (rollback guard): enable runtime guard in staging; fallback to be rate-limited when parity failures exceed threshold. Duration: 2 weeks.
Stage 3 (enforcement): block fallback in production for routes with persistent parity failures >3 days; notify owners and trigger onboarding remediation.
Post-rollout: 1 week monitoring window and retrospective; update SDLC onboarding checklist accordingly.
